findings.title: Pricing Requirements
findings.fact: Prices are to be provided by the Bidder on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form. A Bidder’s failure to provide a complete pricing response will result in the Bidder’s proposal being deemed non-responsive. Bidders must not modify or change the Attachment. Any pricing information or add-on costs that do not conform to the presentation allowed on Attachment 1 cannot be evaluated, will be disregarded as extraneous, and cannot be charged to the Department. Charges for travel cannot be listed as separate line items on the bid response form. The prices bid for each item must be inclusive of all costs. Prices as they appear on submitted bids must be guaranteed by the vendor for the term of the Agreement.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must strictly adhere to the pricing format in Attachment 1. Any deviation or incomplete pricing will lead to disqualification. All costs, including travel, must be included in the unit prices, and prices are fixed for the two-year term.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully complete Attachment 1, ensuring all required pricing fields are filled and no modifications are made. Include all costs (e.g., travel, installation) in the per-device prices. Double-check that the total costs are accurate and competitive, as they cannot be changed later.

quotes.quote: Prices are to be provided by the Bidder on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form. findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your company is registered for electronic payments with the NYS Comptroller's office before contract commencement. Familiarize yourself with the invoice submission process and requirements. Maintain accurate records to ensure invoices do not exceed bid amounts unless changes are approved in writing.

quotes.quote: Payment for invoices submitted by the awarded Bidder shall only be rendered electronically unless payment by paper check is expressly authorized by the Commissioner, at the Commissioner’s sole discretion, due to extenuating circumstances. findings.title: Installation Costs
findings.fact: All installation costs must be provided on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form, and must be inclusive of all labor and travel to the Department’s three (3) locations. The cost must include any additional items required for proper installation (i.e., cables, zip ties, harnesses).
findings.business_implication: The bidder must carefully estimate all installation-related expenses, including labor, travel to three locations, and ancillary materials, to avoid underbidding and potential financial losses.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct a thorough cost analysis for installation at each of the three specified locations, including travel time, labor hours, and materials. Ensure all costs are itemized and included in the Quote Response Form to avoid post-award disputes.

quotes.quote: All installation costs must be provided on Attachment 1, Quote Response Form, and must be inclusive of all labor and travel to the Department’s three (3) locations. The cost must include any additional items required for proper installation (i.e., cables, zip ties, harnesses).

findings.title: Set-Off Rights
findings.fact: The State shall have all of its common law, equitable and statutory rights of set-off, including the option to withhold moneys due to the Contractor under this contract up to any amounts due and owing to the State with regard to this contract, any other contract with any State department or agency, plus any amounts due and owing to the State for any other reason including tax delinquencies, fee delinquencies or monetary penalties.
findings.business_implication: The State can withhold payments due to the contractor for any debts the contractor owes to the State, not just those related to this contract. This creates a financial risk for the contractor, as payments under this contract could be offset by unrelated obligations.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the contractor's financial obligations to the State to ensure there are no outstanding debts that could trigger set-off. Maintain accurate records and consider negotiating limitations on set-off rights, though this may be difficult given the standard nature of the clause.

quotes.quote: 9. SET-OFF RIGHTS.  The State shall have all of its common law, equitable and statutory rights of set-off.  These rights shall include, but not be limited to, the State's option to withhold for the purposes of set-off any moneys due to the Contractor under this contract up to any amounts due and owing to the State with regard to this contract, any other contract with any State department or agency, including any contract for a term commencing prior to the term of this contract, plus any  amounts  due  and  owing  to  the  State for  any  other  reason  including,  without  limitation,  tax  delinquencies,  fee  delinquencies  or monetary penalties relative thereto.  The State shall exercise its set-off rights in accordance with normal State practices including, in cases of set-off pursuant  to  an  audit,  the  finalization  of  such  audit  by  the  State agency,  its  representatives,  or the  State Comptroller.

findings.title: Contract Void Without Workers' Compensation Coverage
findings.fact: The contract shall be void and of no force and effect unless the Contractor provides and maintains workers' compensation coverage during the life of the contract.

findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that workers' compensation insurance is in place before contract execution and maintained throughout the contract term. Provide proof of coverage as required and monitor renewal dates to avoid lapses.

quotes.quote: In accordance with Section 142 of the State Finance Law, this contract shall be void and of no force and effect unless the Contractor shall provide and maintain coverage during the life of this contract for the benefit of such employees as are required to be covered by the provisions of the Workers' Compensation Law.

findings.title: State's Broad Set-Off Rights
findings.fact: The State has the right to withhold any moneys due to the Contractor under this contract for amounts owed to the State under any contract or for any reason, including tax delinquencies and penalties.
findings.business_implication: The State's set-off rights are extremely broad, allowing it to withhold payments for any debts the contractor owes to the State, even if unrelated to this contract. This increases the contractor's financial risk and could impact cash flow.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct a thorough review of the contractor's financial obligations to the State to identify any potential set-off risks. Consider setting aside contingency funds to mitigate the impact of potential withholdings. Additionally, ensure all tax and fee obligations are current to avoid triggering set-off.

quotes.quote: The State shall have all of its common law, equitable and statutory rights of set-off. These rights shall include, but not be limited to, the State's option to withhold for the purposes of set-off any moneys due to the Contractor under this contract up to any amounts due and owing to the State with regard to this contract, any other contract with any State department or agency, including any contract for a term commencing prior to the term of this contract, plus any amounts due and owing to the State for any other reason including, without limitation, tax delinquencies, fee delinquencies or monetary penalties relative thereto.

findings.title: Ambiguity in Number of Vehicles
findings.fact: The RFQ states an initial order of 93 GPS devices, but the sum of vehicles listed at the three installation locations is 93 (42+32+19), which is consistent, but the RFQ also notes that the number of vehicles is subject to change, creating ambiguity in the required quantity.
findings.business_implication: The quantity of GPS devices may change, affecting the bidder's pricing and resource allocation. The ambiguity could lead to disputes over the scope of work and pricing adjustments.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify the exact number of devices and the process for changes. Ensure that the pricing structure accounts for potential variations in quantity. Consider including a clause for adjusting prices if quantities change significantly.

quotes.quote: The Department anticipates an initial order of ninety-three (93) GPS devices to be installed at three (3) different locations within New York State.
Please note that the number of vehicles requiring installation at each location are subject to change.
